title: B200 bring-up + initial hardware tuning preset (experimental, gated)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- Early enablement of NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell) for Redwood serving runtime via a versioned hardware tuning profile.
- Deliver an initial preset that is safe-by-default, measurable, and explicitly gated (NOT on by default fleet-wide).

Why this is high risk
- Limited B200 fleet access means we may tune against a small subset of host configs (PCIe vs SXM variance, clocks/power limits, networking, BIOS differences).
- Kernel-selection and scheduler knobs that look good in microbenchmarks can create p95 regressions under realistic prompt distributions (streaming + tool calling + bursty concurrency).
- Software stack requirements are stricter vs H100/L40S and failure modes are less familiar for oncall.

Scope
In scope
- Define B200 assumptions + required software stack (driver/CUDA/NCCL/container runtime).
- Add B200 detection normalization + profile selection (under experimental flag).
- Initial B200 tuning knobs (kernel-selection toggles + scheduler defaults + KV cache / memory guardrails).
- Staged validation + canary plan with explicit rollback.

Out of scope (for initial bring-up)
- New kernels from scratch.
- Customer-specific tuning beyond the standard profile pack.
- MIG-specific optimization beyond “detect + safe fallback” behavior.

Assumptions / Required stack (must be explicit in docs + runtime startup checks)
- NVIDIA Driver: >= 555.xx (preferred 560.xx) on B200 nodes.
- CUDA: 12.5+ runtime libraries available in base image (CUDA 12.4 may work but not supported for initial rollout).
- NCCL: >= 2.22 for multi-GPU hosts; ensure collectives config is consistent with our topology assumptions.
- nvidia-container-toolkit: current fleet baseline; confirm cgroup v2 compatibility.
- Firmware / power: nodes configured to vendor-recommended defaults; record any clocks/power caps in benchmark artifacts.
- If requirements are not met at runtime startup, log a clear “incompatible stack” message and fall back to generic-safe profile (NOT B200 preset).

Definition of Done / Acceptance Criteria
Functional
- Runtime correctly identifies B200 across provider string variants (e.g., "NVIDIA B200", "B200-SXM", instance metadata variations) and selects B200 profile only when gated.
- Runtime startup logs include: detected GPU SKU, chosen profile, profile version, and compatibility checks (driver/CUDA).
- A single feature flag can disable B200 profile per pool/region without redeploying the runtime.

Performance (initial targets; will be tightened once we have stable baselines)
- No worse than H100-balanced profile by >3% on p95 latency in the “balanced” workload matrix buckets that fit on B200.
- Throughput improvement target: +10–20% tokens/sec on representative decode-heavy workloads vs generic profile, subject to stability.
- Zero increase in OOM rate (guardrails must prevent pathological KV cache growth).

Operational
- Canary gates added/updated to segment metrics by selected profile and catch p95/p99 regressions.
- Rollback playbook is documented and validated in one staged rollout (test pool -> small region -> one production pool).

Implementation plan (proposed)
1) Stack validation + guardrails
- Add explicit minimum versions; fail closed (do not enable B200 profile) when ambiguous.
- Add “compatibility matrix” line to startup logs.

2) Initial preset knobs (starting point; expected to iterate)
- Kernel-selection:
  - Enable Blackwell-optimized attention kernels when seq_len buckets indicate benefit; keep conservative defaults for long-context buckets until validated.
  - Preserve a hard escape hatch to use the runtime’s generic kernel auto-select.
- Scheduler:
  - Start from H100-balanced semantics with stricter queue limits to avoid tail-latency blowups.
  - Conservative continuous batching limits until we verify prefill/decode fairness under streaming.
- KV cache / memory:
  - Conservative KV cache reservation and eviction thresholds; prioritize avoiding fragmentation and surprise OOM.
  - Emit metrics for KV cache occupancy and eviction counts, by model and pool.

3) Validation sequence
- Microbench sanity checks (attention kernels, GEMMs) on a pinned model family and seq_len buckets.
- Full workload matrix run (ENG-4827 harness): streaming + non-streaming; tool-calling patterns; concurrency sweeps.
- Perf-canary: gate on p95/p99, error rate, OOM, and config drift signals.

4) Rollout plan (must remain staged)
- Keep B200 profile behind: runtime.profiles.b200.experimental=true
- Enable only in a dedicated canary pool first.
- Expand to one region pool with explicit rollback thresholds.
- Do not enable in EU pools until we have at least one stable week of canary + infra sign-off.

Links / Artifacts
- Epic: ENG-4821
- Schema + loader prerequisites: ENG-4822, ENG-4823
- Perf suite: ENG-4827
- Canary gates: ENG-4828
- Related implementation PR (expected): redwood/pr-22021-b200-experimental-profile-flag-and-defaults

Risks / Open questions
- Fleet access: how many distinct B200 host configs do we have this cycle (SXM vs PCIe, NVLink domains, NIC types)? Need Infra to confirm.
- Version churn: if CUDA/driver constraints change mid-cycle, we need a single source of truth and a crisp fallback message.
- Multi-GPU + NCCL: what is the minimum tested topology for initial bring-up? If not tested, disable multi-GPU path or force conservative collectives defaults.
- Benchmark realism: ensure Applied ML reviewers sign off on prompt distribution coverage before promoting beyond canary.

Owner checklist
- [ ] Confirm B200 node images meet driver/CUDA/NCCL requirements and document exact versions used in benchmarks.
- [ ] Implement startup compatibility checks and fallback behavior.
- [ ] Land initial preset knobs behind experimental flag.
- [ ] Run workload matrix on B200 and publish summary artifact.
- [ ] Add canary dashboards segmented by profile selection.
- [ ] Write rollout/rollback notes for oncall; validate disable switch works per pool.
comments: 2025-11-19 (Isabella Rossi): Met with Infra (Irene/Vanessa) — B200 access is limited to a small canary pool. We’ll treat this as “experimental only” through at least runtime-1.18 and require explicit pool opt-in.

2025-11-21 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler defaults should start conservative. We’ve seen tail latency regressions on H100 when pushing fairness knobs too far; for B200 bring-up prioritize stability and observability over peak tokens/sec.

2025-11-25 (Rina Kobayashi): Perf suite runner is ready to enumerate workload matrix; B200 jobs need pinned container image with CUDA 12.5 libs. Please publish exact image digest used so results are reproducible.

2025-12-02 (Neha Kapoor): SRE requirement: single toggle to disable B200 profile per pool/region + startup logs must make it obvious which profile is active. Also need explicit rollback thresholds for p95 and error rate before expanding beyond canary.

2025-12-06 (Isabella Rossi): Drafted initial assumptions + minimum versions. Next step is to land runtime checks + gated profile defaults (targeting PR redwood/pr-22021). Will not enable EU pools until canary is stable and perf-canary noise is addressed.
